column6: description

Practices social-technical software engineering methods and tools to solve real-world problems. Explores innovative design and programming techniques to build significant business applications quickly. Studies the process of systematically combining UX techniques, business processes, and complex data models to assemble applications that are user-friendly and meet business requirements. Employs the object-oriented paradigm, visual user interface design principles, and programming languages such as Java, as well as productivity tools, to put together complicated, powerful business applications with ease. Explores the art of how to systematically write software programs to solve any business problem, through practicing simple and smart ways of making software programming enjoyable.

column5: Boston | Portland, Maine | Silicon Valley, CA | Toronto, Canada | Arlington, VA | Vancouver, Canada | Miami, FL | Online | Seattle, WA
column6: Takes students in a step-by-step manner through the process of systematically combining UX techniques, business processes, and complex data models to assemble applications that are user-friendly and meet business requirements. Employs the object-oriented paradigm, visual user experience, and system design principles to put together complicated, powerful, real-world applications. The primary objective of this course is to practice social-technical software engineering methods and tools to solve real-world problems. Offers students an opportunity to learn innovative design and programming techniques to build significant business applications quickly; to practice simple and smart ways of making software construction enjoyable; and to master the art of how to systematically write software programs to solve any business problem. Corequisite: INFO 5101 (must be taken concurrently).

column5: Online | Portland, Maine | Seattle, WA | Silicon Valley, CA | Toronto, Canada | Arlington, VA | Vancouver, Canada | Miami, FL
column6: Accompanies INFO 5100. Provides additional instruction in Java programming. Corequisite: INFO 5100 (must be taken concurrently).

column2: Data Science Engineering Methods and Tools
column5: Boston | Seattle, WA | Silicon Valley, CA | Vancouver, Canada | Online | Oakland, CA
column6: Introduces the fundamental techniques for machine learning and data science engineering. Discusses a variety of machine learning algorithms, along with examples of their implementation, evaluation, and best practices. Lays the foundation of how learning models are derived from complex data pipelines, both algorithmically and practically. Topics include supervised learning (parametric/nonparametric algorithms, support vector machines, kernels, neural networks, deep learning) and unsupervised learning (clustering, dimensionality reduction, recommender systems). Based on numerous real-world case studies.

column2: Web Design and User Experience Engineering
column5: Boston | Seattle, WA | Toronto, Canada | Vancouver, Canada | Arlington, VA
column6: Focuses on advanced user interface engineering, with a strong emphasis on utility and personalized user experiences development. Through the use of tools like React and Flutter, explores how to engineer highly personalized web applications tailored to individual user needs and preferences. Topics include responsive layouts, interactive elements, animation integration, and performance tuning. Offers students an opportunity to gain hands-on experience in building interfaces that dynamically adapt to user behavior, preferences, and context, ensuring a unique and engaging experience for each user.

column5: Boston | Seattle, WA | Online | Silicon Valley, CA | Vancouver, Canada | Toronto, Canada | Arlington, VA | Oakland, CA
column6: Presents data structures and related algorithms, beginning with a brief review of dynamic memory allocation. Discusses the fundamental data structures in detail, including the abstract representation, supporting algorithms, and implementation methods. Focuses on understanding the application of the abstract data structure and the circumstances that affect implementation decisions. Covers lists, stacks, queues, trees, hash tables, and graphs. Covers recursion and searching and sorting algorithms in detail. Emphasizes data abstraction and encapsulation in code design. Explores external storage structures, time permitting.

column5: Vancouver, Canada | Silicon Valley, CA | Seattle, WA | Portland, Maine | Toronto, Canada | Arlington, VA | Oakland, CA
column6: Covers computer information systems and the decision-making process, determination of information requirements, system development life cycle, and system modeling and analysis. Uses a hands-on approach to introduce the student to software engineering methodologies and practices, business requirements specification, business process design, model-driven object-oriented design, software development, and maintenance. Emphasizes the effective leverage of the Unified Modeling Language (UML) to transform business issues and objectives to concrete software solutions that meet business needs and usability and user interface design as critical elements of a successful software engineering engagement.

column2: Planning and Managing Information Systems Development
column6: Provides an overview of the most popular information systems needs’ assessment methodologies including portfolio analysis, stage assessment, business systems planning, and the Alloway survey technique. Topics include utilities IS strategic plan prioritization techniques of business goal alignment, architectural compatibility, and cost/benefit and risk analysis to demonstrate how businesses match needs to budgetary constraints. Describes and evaluates options for the placement of the IS function within the organization and a variety of methods to manage the function. Introduces a generic application development and project planning methodology used as a model to facilitate the development of a four-stage project plan for a prototype project. Uses the Project Management Institute’s PMBOK and Harvard Business School case studies extensively.

Examines techniques for the management and evolution of software systems. Topics include managing software as an asset; life cycle development and rapid development technologies; maintainability; quality assurance of software systems including testing strategies and problem analysis; software risk analysis; analysis of software project failures; process models, such as CMM and ISO 9001; configuration management; and the impact of new development technologies on software management.

Covers application development for mobile devices using advanced development platforms. Focuses on how to write mobile applications using cross-platform development tools and processes. Topics include user interfaces, the software life cycle, persistent storage, networking using HTTP and other REST interfaces, and mobile/handheld data applications. Requires a final project.

Explores approaches for using artificial intelligence to improve the development, evaluation, and performance of other AI systems. Discusses automated feedback, iterative model refinement, and the analysis of model behavior. Examines how AI-assisted workflows can support experimentation, identify limitations, and improve the reliability of intelligent applications.

Presents an in-depth study of risk management in engineering and technical environments, focusing on identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks. Covers strategies for monitoring and response planning while examining the impact of organizational factors, such as communication and culture, on risk practices. Emphasizes real-world applications through case studies and emerging risk assessments. Explores approaches to implementing security controls, developing incident response plans, and ensuring compliance with industry standards.

column2: Accounting and Budgetary Systems for Engineers
column6: Covers the latest engineering principles necessary for building complex software systems that comply with recognized standards in the financial industry. With automated business processes today, risk and responsibility are shifting to information technology (IT) systems. Offers students an opportunity to learn how to incorporate information-based controls related to the financial industry that signal trouble, detect violations, and provide accountability, as well as a working approval process. Emphasizes software design. Seeks to help engineers construct complex software from a sophisticated engineering perspective. Examines how to put together cutting-edge organizational systems that people in the financial world can put to good use. Designed to prepare students for jobs in the building, maintaining, and employment of such information systems.

Introduces the engineering of software systems used to support trading workflows and financial transactions. Examines how market data, application logic, and system architecture interact in trading environments. Discusses reliability, performance, testing, and the challenges of designing systems that process rapidly changing financial information.

Explores advanced methods for developing applications with large language models. Examines prompt design, retrieval-based techniques, model adaptation, and the evaluation of generated responses. Discusses ways to improve the accuracy, efficiency, and reliability of LLM-enabled systems and considers practical challenges in integrating language models into software applications.

column2: ST: Security GRC in the AI Era
column6: Examines the relationship between cybersecurity governance, risk management, compliance, and the adoption of artificial intelligence. Discusses AI-related security concerns, organizational controls, and methods for assessing risks in intelligent systems. Explores how policies, monitoring practices, and regulatory considerations shape the responsible deployment of AI technologies.

Explores the application of information systems engineering methods to interdisciplinary problems encountered in industry. Emphasizes the translation of organizational needs into technical requirements and the coordination of work across different areas of expertise. Discusses project planning, communication, solution design, and the evaluation of practical engineering outcomes.

Introduces techniques for designing effective prompts and developing AI applications that perform tasks through coordinated reasoning and tool use. Explores prompt structure, context management, and the behavior of large language models in multistep workflows. Discusses the design, evaluation, and reliability of agent-based systems for practical applications.

Focuses on the engineering of applications that incorporate artificial intelligence capabilities. Examines how models, application interfaces, data sources, and backend services work together in an integrated system. Discusses prototyping, system design, model evaluation, and the practical challenges of making AI-enabled software useful, reliable, and maintainable.

column2: ST: User Exp in Era of Gen AI
column6: Explores user experience design for products and services that incorporate generative artificial intelligence. Examines how conversational interactions, generated content, and adaptive interfaces influence user expectations and behavior. Discusses usability, transparency, user control, and methods for evaluating the experience of interacting with AI-powered applications.

Introduces methods for connecting user experience design with the engineering of interactive software systems. Examines how user needs, interface structures, and application behavior inform technical design decisions. Discusses prototyping, accessibility, usability evaluation, and iterative improvement in the development of digital products.

Examines data engineering practices that support artificial intelligence and machine learning applications. Covers data collection, cleaning, transformation, storage, and the organization of data pipelines for model development. Discusses data quality, scalability, and the challenges of preparing reliable datasets for training, evaluation, and deployment.

column2: ST: High Perf Computing for AI
column6: Explores computing techniques and system architectures used to support computationally intensive AI workloads. Examines parallel processing, resource utilization, and the performance characteristics of model training and inference. Discusses how hardware and software design choices affect the efficiency, scalability, and reliability of AI applications.

Examines approaches for developing AI systems that use feedback and evaluation to improve their performance over time. Explores iterative refinement, automated assessment, and techniques for identifying weaknesses in model outputs or application behavior. Discusses reliability, validation, and the challenges of measuring meaningful improvement in intelligent systems.

Explores how large language models represent, interpret, and use meaning in text and structured information. Examines semantic relationships, context, information retrieval, and methods for connecting language-model outputs to relevant knowledge. Discusses applications in question answering, information organization, and the development of more context-aware AI systems.

Introduces approaches that combine neural learning methods with symbolic representations and reasoning. Examines how data-driven models can interact with structured knowledge, rules, and logical relationships. Discusses system design considerations for building AI applications that integrate pattern recognition with explicit reasoning and interpretable representations.

Explores methods for critically evaluating computational results and the claims made by AI systems. Examines uncertainty, conflicting evidence, model limitations, and the assessment of information quality. Discusses techniques for testing assumptions, verifying outputs, and designing software workflows that support careful interpretation of machine-generated results.

Introduces neural network models and their role in contemporary artificial intelligence applications. Examines network architectures, model training, optimization, and approaches to evaluating predictive performance. Discusses the strengths and limitations of neural methods and their use in solving classification, prediction, and representation-learning problems.

column2: ST: System Design in Age of AI
column6: Most engineers can name architectural patterns. Fewer can choose the right one under pressure and defend that choice in a room full of skeptics. This course closes that gap. Each week, you will study a real-world systems architecture in depth, in production — understanding not just what it is, but why it exists, when and how it breaks down, and what it is actually optimized for. You deploy a prototype implementation. Then you break it and rebuild it. Using AI as your results analyzer and implementation co-pilot and working in teams, you will deploy a working version of each architecture on AWS and by breaking it learn to recognize the failure modes that interviewers love to probe. By the end of the semester, you will not have opinions about systems design — you will have hands-on evidence. Note that this class does not focus on running production service lines on public Clouds. There is another class that I will teach in the Spring focusing on this. This class focuses on the System Design aspect of Software development. But you cannot study a Design without seeing it in production.

Explores architectural approaches for integrating artificial intelligence into enterprise software environments. Examines how AI services interact with organizational data, application interfaces, and existing business systems. Discusses integration patterns, security, governance, scalability, and the engineering challenges of deploying AI capabilities across an organization.

column2: ST: Forward Deploy Engr for AI
column6: Examines the engineering work involved in adapting and integrating AI solutions within real organizational environments. Explores requirements gathering, data integration, application customization, and collaboration with end users. Discusses how deployment constraints, feedback, testing, and ongoing iteration shape the delivery of practical AI systems.

Focuses on communication strategies and tactics for engineers at the interpersonal, team, and organizational level. Course topics include forms (oral and written), styles, and differences in communication; coaching and giving feedback to staff; and building teams, managing conflict, and special topics in organizational communication. The primary goal is to strengthen the students’ social and emotional intelligence skills to help them progress along their engineering career path. Combines academic content with practical skill-building activities.

column2: Advances in Data Sciences and Architecture
column6: Covers a wide range of skills and responsibilities that are necessary for managing complex business performance and operational data. Such data tend to be fragmented, poorly organized, and often flawed. Offers students an opportunity to learn how a more up-to-date mapping of complex data works and to be alerted to the care and attention they must give to such a task as well as the implications of the results. Covers best practices for managing all aspects of the data transformation life cycle, covering broad areas such as requirements gathering, meta-model design, data integration and transformation, as well as implementation and ongoing operations. Discusses tools for mapping fragmented data into business intelligence solutions that guide successful strategies.

Offers students an opportunity to achieve an advanced level of practical knowledge and understanding of the medical device software development process and the skills needed to develop software for medical devices according to the FDA and IEC 62304 standards. Aiming to bridge the gap between theory and practice, this comprehensive and hands-on course combines lectures, case studies, and a capstone project to help students gain the necessary expertise to develop safe and effective medical device software.

Examines the architecture and security of enterprise applications built around AI agents. Explores how autonomous components interact with organizational systems, tools, and data services. Discusses access control, secure integration, monitoring, risk management, and the challenges of deploying reliable agent-based workflows in enterprise environments.

Delves deeply into advanced concepts and methodologies within information systems. Emphasizes the development of critical thinking skills and the application of theoretical knowledge to practical challenges in the field. Through individual efforts, including laboratory work and/or literature review, students conduct a thorough investigation and analysis of various aspects of information systems. With guidance from their faculty advisor, students focus on a project tailored to their interests and goals. Students produce a detailed report outlining their findings, methodologies, and conclusions. Offers students an opportunity to present their work to peers and faculty, fostering scholarly discussion and collaboration.
